posts.title: Why investors look at the Coast
posts.socialPost:
Why do investors look at the Mississippi Gulf Coast? Steady military renters near Keesler and the Seabee base, year-round visitors, and prices below many beach markets. The catch: insurance. Good Coast deals price it in from day one.

More in my Investor Corner: https://www.billtemplerealtor.com/investors.html#why-the-coast

posts.title: Long-term rentals
posts.socialPost:
Buying a rental on the Coast? The tax bill on the listing is often the seller's homestead bill. Rentals don't get the homestead exemption in Mississippi, so your taxes can be noticeably higher. Get the real number before you make an offer.

More in my Investor Corner: https://www.billtemplerealtor.com/investors.html#long-term-rentals

posts.title: Vacation and short-term rentals
posts.socialPost:
Thinking about an Airbnb on the Mississippi Gulf Coast? Check the city's short-term rental rules and the HOA rules before you buy, not after. And remember the busy summer season overlaps hurricane season, so line up insurance early.

More in my Investor Corner: https://www.billtemplerealtor.com/investors.html#vacation-rentals

posts.title: Fix and flip
posts.socialPost:
Flipping a house on the Gulf Coast? If it's in a high-risk flood zone and the repairs are about half the building's value or more, you may have to bring it up to current flood rules, even elevate it. Check with the building department before you buy.

More in my Investor Corner: https://www.billtemplerealtor.com/investors.html#flips

posts.title: How to size up a deal
posts.socialPost:
Investor math in plain English: cap rate compares properties as if you paid cash. Cash-on-cash tells you what YOUR money earns. The 1% rule is a quick screen, not a verdict. On the Gulf Coast, always run the numbers with a real insurance quote.

More in my Investor Corner: https://www.billtemplerealtor.com/investors.html#deal-math

posts.title: Coast costs: flood, wind and taxes
posts.socialPost:
Three costs that make or break a Gulf Coast rental: wind coverage (and the hurricane deductible), flood insurance, and property taxes without the homestead exemption. Get real quotes during your inspection period, before your earnest money is at risk.

More in my Investor Corner: https://www.billtemplerealtor.com/investors.html#coast-costs

posts.title: Financing an investment property
posts.socialPost:
Financing a rental is different from buying your own home: usually more down, a slightly higher rate, and reserves in the bank. DSCR loans qualify on the property's rent. Living in one side of a duplex can open other options. Talk to a lender before you shop.

More in my Investor Corner: https://www.billtemplerealtor.com/investors.html#financing
